title: Derived-unit representatives and cross-site hypercover chain squares
statement:
Let $h:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with small pro-etale sites and compatible universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R,R'$ be sheaves of commutative rings with a specified isomorphism $h^{-1}R\cong R'$, giving the actual exact module inverse image $h^*$ and its adjoint $h_*$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $U_\bullet\to X$ and $V_\bullet\to X'$ be augmented simplicial site objects [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], with maps $g_p:V_p\to U_p$ over $h$ commuting with every simplicial operator and augmentation. No matching-cover, weak-contractibility or cartesian-square assumption is imposed. Let $E$ be a strictly bounded-below complex of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and choose quasi-isomorphisms $i:E\to I$ and $j:h^*E\to J$ into strictly bounded-below termwise-injective module complexes. Use the signed totals $T_U,T_V$ and their actual restriction augmentations $\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-total, def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-augmentation]. Write $Q$ for localization into the relevant ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and compute right derived functors with K-injective resolutions [def-sfb-right-derived-functor].

There is a chain map $b:h^*I\to J$, unique up to homotopy subject to $b h^*i\simeq j$. For every such $b$, let $a=h_*b\circ\eta_I:I\to h_*J$, where $\eta$ is the specified ordinary adjunction unit. Then $h_*J$ is K-injective and $ai\simeq h_*j\circ\eta_E$. Under the canonical resolution identifications, $Qa\circ Qi$ represents the actual derived adjunction unit $QE\to Rh_*h^*QE$. Consequently the chain map $\Gamma(a):I(X)\to J(X')$, with $\Gamma(X,h_*J)=\Gamma(X',J)$, represents the canonical unit-induced derived section map $R\Gamma(X,QE)\to R\Gamma(X',h^*QE)$. Here the composition comparison for derived direct images is the canonical one, evaluated using the identity resolution of the K-injective $h_*J$, not a chosen isomorphism of functors.

Restriction along $g$ gives a chain map $c_{g,E}:T_U(E)\to T_V(h^*E)$. Define $G:T_U(I)\to T_V(J)$ on bidegree $(p,q)$ by restriction along $g_p$ followed by $b^q$. These are chain maps for the differential $\delta+(-1)^p d$, and satisfy
$$G\alpha_I=\alpha_J\Gamma(a)\quad\text{strictly},\qquad G T_U(i)\simeq T_V(j)c_{g,E}.$$
If $s:b h^*i\simeq j$ is a coefficient homotopy, the latter homotopy on bidegree $(p,q)$ is $(-1)^p$ times restriction along $g_p$ followed by $s^q$.

The maps $c_{g,E}$ commute strictly with coefficient chain maps and with refinements whenever the augmented simplicial diagrams commute. For consecutive scheme maps and consecutive augmented simplicial maps they commute with composition and identity after the canonical coefficient and ordinary pullback comparisons [def-sfb-proetale-composite-coefficients, def-sfb-proetale-ordinary-pullback-comparison]. Explicitly, identifying $(hk)^*E\cong k^*h^*E$, the composite of the degree-$p$ restrictions is the restriction along the composite degree-$p$ map; thus $c_{g',h^*E}c_{g,E}=c_{gg',E}$.

Injective objects and resolutions are as in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; coefficient homotopies and K-injectivity are as in [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

proof.text: Both $I$ and $J$ are K-injective by bounded-below termwise injectivity. Exactness of $h^*$ implies that $h^*i:h^*E\to h^*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the K-injective comparison principle with target $J$: precomposition with $h^*i$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(h^*I,J)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(h^*E,J)$. The preimage of $[j]$ has a chain representative $b$, and bijectivity says exactly that all admissible $b$ have the same homotopy class. Thus there is a coefficient homotopy $s$ with $b h^*i-j=d_Js+s d_{h^*E}$.

For an acyclic module complex $A$ on $X$, exactness makes $h^*A$ acyclic. The termwise homotopy adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(A,h_*J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(h^*A,J)=0$. This is precisely K-injectivity of $h_*J$; no assertion that $h^*I$ is injective is needed.

source.place: Label lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives: its displayed Hom argument.

proof.text: The termwise unit is a chain map, hence so is $a=h_*b\,\eta_I$. Naturality gives $\eta_I i=h_*h^*i\,\eta_E$, and therefore $ai=h_*(b h^*i)\eta_E\simeq h_*j\eta_E$. Explicitly the homotopy is $h_*s\,\eta_E$, since additive direct image preserves the differential identity defining $s$.

source.place: Label lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, termwise adjunction; explicit naturality calculation.

proof.text: Use the actual canonical adjunction of def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, which is now the source library mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction of the normalized ordinary module adjunction. Its Mathlib derived unit equation derivedη_fac_app on the homotopy category states ηD(Qh E) followed by Rh_*(φh_E) equals Qh(η_E) followed by the right-derived unit. The proved cochain normalization lemma [lem-sfb-derived-adjunction-cochain-unit] transports this equation along quotientCompQhIso and mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh_hom_app to obtain ηD(QE) followed by Rh_*(φ_E) = Q(η_E) followed by γ_(h^*E). Naturality of γ at j then gives Q(transpose j) followed by γ_J = ηD(QE) followed by Rh_*(φ_E followed by Qj). Apply the localized homotopy from step 3 to replace Q(transpose j) by Qi followed by Q(transpose b). All units and factorizations are the published canonical constructions; no existential choice of a derived adjunction is used.

proof.text: Evaluate the universal normalization of the source library rightDerivedFunctorCompIso' for F=h_* and G=Gamma_X. Its homotopy-category unit equation follows directly from rightDerivedUnique and rightDerivedNatTrans_app. Transport along quotientCompQhIso to obtain γ_G(FJ) followed by RG(γ_F(J)) followed by the canonical composition comparison = γ_(FG)(J). The literal equality Gamma_X h_*=Gamma_Y identifies the last unit with γ_Y(J). Naturality of γ_X at any a:I→h_*J gives sections_composition_representative, without a K-injectivity hypothesis. For sections_representative, the units at I and J are invertible by bounded-below injectivity. Apply RGamma_X to the equality of step 4, use naturality of the composition comparison, and cancel the invertible RGamma_X(Qi). This gives exactly the displayed canonical derived section map.

proof.text: For a module sheaf $F$ and $g_p:V_p\to U_p$, let $\widetilde g_p:V_p\to X\!\prime\times_XU_p$ be its factorization through the fibre product. Define $r_p^F:F(U_p)\to(h^*F)(V_p)$ as the section of the module unit at $U_p$, followed by restriction along $\widetilde g_p$. It is natural in $F$. The simplicial commutation assumption and the restriction identity $(uv)^*=v^*u^*$ give $r_{p+1}^F d_i^*=d_i^*r_p^F$ for every face. The same equality holds for degeneracies. Thus $r$ commutes with the alternating sum $\delta$ and with coefficient differentials. Applying it in every bidegree defines $c_{g,E}$, and composing it with $b^q$ defines $G$. Both commute with $\delta+(-1)^p d$ and so induce the asserted chain maps on the signed totals.

source.place: Label lemma-compute-cohomology, section bicomplex; explicit cross-site restriction using the specified adjunction.

proof.text: For $x\in I^q(X)$, both $G\alpha_I(x)$ and $\alpha_J\Gamma(a)(x)$ lie in bidegree $(0,q)$. The first is $b^q_{V_0}r_0^{I^q}(x|_{U_0})$. By naturality of the unit with respect to restriction and commutativity of the augmented diagram, this equals $b^q_{V_0}((\eta_Ix)|_{V_0})$. By naturality of the sheaf map $b^q$ it equals $(b^q_{X\prime}\eta_Ix)|_{V_0}$, which is the second expression. All other bidegrees are zero, giving $G\alpha_I=\alpha_J\Gamma(a)$ strictly.

source.place: Label lemma-compute-cohomology, actual restriction augmentations; explicit evaluation of the square.

proof.text: On bidegree $(p,q)$ put $H=(-1)^p s^q_{V_p}r_p^{E^q}$, of total degree $-1$. Naturality of restriction makes $s$ commute with the coface restrictions. In $DH+HD$, for $D=\delta+(-1)^p d$, the horizontal terms cancel because their signs are $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$. The vertical terms have sign $(-1)^{2p}=1$ and sum to $(d_Js+s d_{h^*E})r_p^E=(b h^*i-j)r_p^E$. Naturality in the coefficient map $i$ identifies this with the bidegree component of $GT_U(i)-T_V(j)c_{g,E}$. Therefore $H$ is precisely the required homotopy. The total degree sums have finite support because the complexes are strictly bounded below.

source.place: Label lemma-compute-cohomology, signed total model; agent calculation of the coefficient homotopy sign.

proof.text: For a coefficient chain map $t:E\to F$, naturality of the ordinary unit and of section restriction gives $(h^*t)_{V_p}r_p^E=r_p^Ft_{U_p}$ in every bidegree. Hence $T_V(h^*t)c_{g,E}=c_{g,F}T_U(t)$ strictly. For refinements on the two sides, a commuting augmented simplicial diagram says the two degree-$p$ composite scheme maps coincide; functoriality of the restrictions in the definition of $r_p$ gives equality of the degree-$p$ section maps. Their total maps are therefore equal, with no appeal to a comparison isomorphism of cohomology groups.

source.place: Label lemma-compute-cohomology, functorial restriction model; explicit coefficient and refinement equalities.

proof.text: For consecutive maps $Z\xrightarrow{k}X\prime\xrightarrow{h}X$, write $A:(hk)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}k^*h^*$ and $B:h_*k_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(hk)_*$ for the specified ordinary comparisons. The definition of $A$ as the mate of $B$ means, on a coefficient sheaf $F$, that $B_{k^*h^*F}\,h_*(\eta^k_{h^*F})\,\eta^h_F=(hk)_*(A_F)\eta^{hk}_F$. Evaluate this equality at $U_p$, then restrict to the degree-$p$ object on $Z$. The section formula for $B$ is exactly fibre-product pasting. The resulting equality says that restriction along $g_p$ followed by that along $g_p\prime$ equals restriction along $g_pg_p\prime$ after $A_F$. The composite coefficient action is exactly the specified composite ring identification. This holds termwise for $F=E^q$, hence $c_{g\prime,h^*E}c_{g,E}=c_{gg\prime,E}$ after the stated comparisons. For an identity map the direct-image pasting map is identity; its mate identifies its unit with identity, so the same calculation gives the identity total map.
